nodes.text: The same A-then-B import order can arise from Porto-to-Oslo or Oslo-to-Porto event histories. The actual current city is underdetermined; an additional later move is also compatible with the inputs.
nodes.quote: Same two statements, same import order, opposite answers, because import order and event order are independent.
nodes.verification: Compared the two constructed histories against the stated inputs. Neither requires import order to equal event order. This is a synthetic logical counterexample, not a measurement of a real person's location.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; reasoning review, no external model identity verification

nodes.text: A date on only one conflicting assertion does not generally order both. A document date need not be the event date, and knowing the last recorded value still does not prove the actual current value without assumptions about later changes.
nodes.quote: Any ONE of the following would permit an answer:
nodes.verification: Counterexample to sufficiency: keep A at event time 10; B may have occurred at 5 or 20. Both possibilities agree with the single known date but reverse the latest recorded value. Full temporal/provenance assumptions must be declared. No experiment was run for this reasoning review.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; reasoning review, no external model identity verification

nodes.text: Strictly separated event-time bounds suffice to order the two represented events, conditional on valid bounds on a common time scale. This is not a globally minimal metadata requirement: direct relative-order evidence can also suffice.
nodes.quote: Let the event times lie in closed uncertainty intervals [lA,uA] and [lB,uB], with uA strictly less than lB.
nodes.verification:
Reasoned that tA <= uA < lB <= tB implies tA < tB for every compatible assignment. This adds evidence absent from the original undated inputs and does not validate the bounds themselves. No execution occurred.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: Ordering represented events does not establish source truthfulness or actual current residence. A later unrecorded move remains compatible; a current-state conclusion requires trustworthy query-time evidence or justified persistence and coverage assumptions.
nodes.quote: The supplied Porto-then-Oslo record remains compatible with a later unrecorded move to Lisbon, so it does not settle the current city.
nodes.verification:
Reasoned that histories with and without a subsequent move preserve the same recorded events while differing at query time. Event-occurrence bounds alone do not establish residence validity or reliability. No histories were executed or observations obtained.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: The proposed evaluation separates import order, document dates, event order, reliability and hidden changes, while distinguishing latest-recorded and actual-current targets. The 50 percent baseline is conditional on a balanced pair of import permutations with different values and a fixed event-latest target.
nodes.quote: Proposed synthetic evaluation, not yet executed: hold the recorded event order fixed while permuting import order;
nodes.verification:
Reviewed the proposed controls conceptually. Under the specified balanced two-permutation setup, import-last selects the event-latest value in one permutation out of two. No generator, model comparison or benchmark was executed; the claimed PMC-001 contract was not independently inspected.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: An export retaining active assertions and tombstones but dropping retracted assertion bodies loses ID-collision detection when a changed record with a retired ID arrives. Preserving the present answer and resisting exact duplicates does not establish equivalence under later mutations.
nodes.quote: E resists resurrection (rule 3) but silently loses collision detection (rule 2).
nodes.verification: Operator-authored pilot/review_round1.py reran the published local resolve(): full and compact logs both give Porto before and after an exact duplicate; a mutated b gives invalid in the full log but Porto in the compact log. Eight checks and full synthetic inputs are published in /pilot/review_round1_report.json. No submitted code was executed. This is an example, not a universal proof.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; local reproduction, not an independent outside participant

nodes.text: A collision for another entity or a retraction of a retraction makes the entire ledger invalid under the declared contract. This is an intentional rule with a denial-of-service concern for untrusted writers, not a newly discovered reader implementation bug.
nodes.quote: This is the contract as stated (rule 2 'even outside the queried entity'), not a reader bug
nodes.verification: The controlled reproduction checks a collision for lea while querying mira and a retract-of-retract. Both return invalid. A valid unrelated record does not by itself cause invalidity: the qualifier matters. The reference contract was not changed.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; local reproduction, not an independent outside participant

nodes.text: A per-ID fingerprint plus retained active records and tombstone information is a candidate repair, not yet an established equivalent compact representation. It needs an explicit importer and tests covering record kinds, invalid retractions, cross-entity arrivals, query assumptions and resource limits.
nodes.quote: Invariant: answers equal the full-log answers under any reordering, duplication or late arrival.
nodes.verification: No general equivalence proof or full implementation of the proposed export was supplied in this submission. The reproduced example motivates keeping identity-change information; it does not validate the universal invariant. Distinguish evaluator input-size guards from ledger semantics.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; local reproduction, not an independent outside participant

nodes.text: The necessity of distinguishing certain past records does not prove that every valid representation must store one hash per ID. A finite cryptographic hash is a practical collision-resistant approximation, not an exact injective encoding of arbitrary records. Minimality and collision assumptions must be stated separately.
nodes.quote: a content-change detector, at least a hash
nodes.verification: Logical review of the quantifier: failure of one export does not establish a storage lower bound over all representations. Exact equivalence and computational collision resistance are different guarantees. This is a qualification of the proposal, not a demonstrated cryptographic collision.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; local reproduction, not an independent outside participant

nodes.text: Scoping invalidity to affected IDs or entities could improve isolation, but it defines a different contract. Study it as a separately versioned policy rather than claiming it is a drop-in implementation of the current global-invalidity rules.
nodes.quote: scope invalidity to the colliding ids (poison set)
nodes.verification: No implementation or reproduction of this changed policy was performed in this review. Dependencies between assertions and tombstones need explicit semantics and tests before adopting it.
nodes.reviewer: Codex acting for the project operator; local reproduction, not an independent outside participant

nodes.text: Two two-record histories [a_s, r] and [a_t, r] that differ only in the source string of a permanently retracted assertion give identical answers (unknown/null/[]) but diverge after the identical continuation a_s: unknown for H_s (exact duplicate) versus invalid for H_t (changed record with retired ID). Under the unchanged v1 rules any deterministic, self-contained importer therefore cannot map both histories to the same total state, even for one fixed query. This is a tighter instance of the existing collision-loss counterexample: it needs only one assertion and its retraction, and shows source strings of retired assertions carry required information.
nodes.quote: H_t followed by a_s gives invalid, null, empty evidence: it reuses a with a changed source.
nodes.verification:
The executed report's checks pmc_r3_retired_history_s and pmc_r3_retired_history_t both return unknown/null/[], pmc_r3_retired_s_then_same_event returns unknown/null/[] and pmc_r3_retired_t_then_same_event returns invalid/null/[] on the pinned reference reader with synthetic fixtures. Only these four concrete answers are reproduced. The inference that a deterministic importer must keep distinct states is a reasoned corollary (same state + same event + same query cannot yield two answers) and was not executed against any exporter/importer; no contributor code was run.
Execution ledger: pmc_r3_retired_history_s, pmc_r3_retired_history_t, pmc_r3_retired_s_then_same_event, pmc_r3_retired_t_then_same_event

nodes.text: Generalizing the witness to n disjoint retired IDs each with one of M possible sources gives M^n pairwise distinguishable histories, so any fixed-width total state for an exact, deterministic, self-contained importer under v1 needs at least ceil(n*log2 M) bits. This is a joint-state counting lower bound, not a per-ID layout theorem and not a requirement to store a hash per ID. It also implies a single fixed-length digest plus source-independent metadata cannot be unconditionally exact when the source alphabet exceeds the digest space; exact equivalence and computational collision resistance remain separate guarantees. The bound depends on stated assumptions: no hidden log or external lookup, invalid must be reproduced exactly, and the witnesses must fit the harness's record and byte guards.
nodes.quote: A fixed-width TOTAL state therefore needs at least ceil(n log2 M) bits.
nodes.verification:
Reasoned review of the counting argument: distinctness of every pair of source vectors follows from the n=1 witness applied at any differing coordinate, and the pigeonhole step is standard. The executed report exercises only n=1 with two sources (its limitations list says so); no M^n family, no 257-character source strings and no check against the reference's byte limits were executed. Whether such long source strings are accepted by the published schema/size guards is unverified. Nothing in the report contradicts the bound. This does not exhibit any hash collision and does not bound average-case compression.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: Assertions identical except valid_from 9007199254740992 versus 9007199254740993 (2^53 and 2^53+1), reusing one ID with a retraction between them, must remain distinguishable under the integer-valued v1 rules; the reference reader returns unknown for the exact duplicate and invalid for the off-by-one record. Any fingerprint or canonical-JSON step that converts integers to IEEE-754 binary64 before hashing would collapse this pair and could let a changed record pass as an exact duplicate. The submission attributes the numeric restriction to RFC 8785 section 3.1 and proposes an exact-integer parser with an injective, versioned preimage encoding, or an explicitly narrower new contract.
nodes.quote: A native binary64-number conversion can erase that distinction before hashing.
nodes.verification:
Reproduced narrowly: pmc_r3_large_valid_from_exact_duplicate returns unknown and pmc_r3_large_valid_from_off_by_one returns invalid on the pinned reference reader; pmc_r3_integer_canonical_json_keeps_off_by_one_distinct, an operator-authored check, reports exact_integer_digests_differ=true and binary64_conversion_collapses=true. No specific JCS library, exporter or deployed RESON component was tested, the RFC text was not consulted by this review, and the proposed parser/encoding remains a design proposal.
Execution ledger: pmc_r3_large_valid_from_exact_duplicate, pmc_r3_large_valid_from_off_by_one, pmc_r3_integer_canonical_json_keeps_off_by_one_distinct

nodes.text: The submission fixes one valid query and allows arbitrary future schema-valid records, and correctly scopes its result as a necessary lower bound. It does not propose or validate any compact importer; sufficiency of any export still needs a separate invariant over all allowed continuations and queries, including multi-event interactions, cross-entity collisions and retractions of retractions. The cheapest disconfirmation is the two-history/same-continuation pair, and the submission states what would count as a counterexample (a self-contained deterministic mechanism with identical total state yielding both required answers) versus a change of contract.
nodes.quote: sufficiency of any proposed importer would still require a separate invariant covering all allowed continuations and queries.
nodes.verification:
Logical review of scope statements; consistent with the existing paired-continuation-test finding and with the report's limitations list (sufficiency of any compact representation and general hash-export correctness remain unexercised). No importer was implemented or executed.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: Under the declared order-insensitive contract, permutation invariance is required but does not establish compact-export equivalence under future arrivals. Shuffling an initial history does not test a changed record introduced later.
nodes.quote: Permutation invariance of the full reader is necessary but not sufficient to establish compact-export equivalence under future arrivals.
nodes.verification:
Reasoned from the difference between reordering existing records and extending a history. The submission appropriately qualifies necessity when arrival order has contractual meaning. The supplied execution report supports the existing retired-ID counterexample; it does not establish universal permutation invariance. No new permutation or continuation tests were executed by this review.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: Comparing full and compact representations after identical continuations is a useful proposed falsification method. Comparison must include status, value and evidence under unchanged semantics. Future arrivals are explicitly included, but the allowed query family and coverage of longer continuations remain unspecified.
nodes.quote: The proposed comparison starts with two representations of the same history, appends the same future event to each, and compares complete answers including status and evidence.
nodes.verification:
Logical review supports this design as a way to expose divergent behavior. The supplied report documents one relevant existing example, not execution of this submission's general proposal. A finite passing collection cannot establish equivalence for all future streams or arbitrary new queries, and no minimality proof or new implementation was supplied.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

nodes.text: The reported harness reproduces the four 257-character-source witness answers: unknown, unknown, unknown and invalid, all with null value and empty evidence. It also reports 127 same/changed-source continuation pairs yielding unknown versus invalid with 255 records. The measured four-case dataset and one 127-ID continuation case occupy 2957 and 52738 bytes respectively, below 128 KiB. These concrete checks address the earlier witness-admissibility gap.
nodes.quote: Histories [a_s,r], [a_t,r], [a_s,r,a_s] and [a_t,r,a_s] return unknown, unknown, unknown and invalid respectively
nodes.verification:
Supported narrowly by the named executed_report checks for the four answers, 127 continuation pairs, measured input sizes and oversized-input rejection. This review executed nothing and followed no URLs. The contributor's original script and serialization were not reproduced. The report's limitation saying only n=1 with two sources was exercised conflicts with its newer n127 check; the explicit checks support these finite results, not exhaustive family coverage.
Execution ledger: pmc_bounds_source257, pmc_bounds_n127, pmc_bounds_input_sizes

nodes.text: For the tested 128-retired-ID pair, both 256-record prefixes return unknown and both 257-record continuations return invalid. Thus these particular continuations no longer distinguish the prefixes at the record cap. This limits this construction without establishing a global maximum lower bound.
nodes.quote: At 128 retired IDs both prefixes have 256 records and return unknown; both 257-record continuations return invalid because of the resource cap.
nodes.verification:
pmc_bounds_n128_cap records the four answers and record counts. Reproduction is limited to those concrete outputs. The conclusion that this continuation supplies no distinguishing answer is reasoned from their equality; no alternative construction or global optimization was executed.
Execution ledger: pmc_bounds_n128_cap

nodes.text: Conditional on the described source validation, unchanged v1 semantics and admissible continuations, 127 independently chosen 257-bit sources give 2^32639 pairwise distinguishable prefixes. Appending the assertion from one vector at a differing coordinate yields unknown for that vector and invalid for the other. An exact deterministic self-contained importer therefore requires at least 32639 bits of fixed-width total state for this family, including all source-dependent metadata. One fixed query suffices for this argument. It establishes neither a per-ID storage layout nor compact-export sufficiency.
nodes.quote: A fixed-width total state therefore needs at least 32639 bits for this family.
nodes.verification:
Reasoned by counting 2^(127*257) source vectors and applying the same-state, same-continuation, same-query contradiction to each differing pair. Equal-length binary source strings preserve the described serialization length; admissibility of the entire family remains conditional on the stated validation rules, which this review did not inspect. No exhaustive enumeration, hash collision search, exporter/importer execution or equivalence proof was performed. Arbitrary new queries are unnecessary for this lower bound but remain an unresolved exporter requirement.
Execution ledger: No execution attributed to this finding; reasoning only.

edges.reason: Preserves the valid counterexample while correcting the overly broad proposed condition for resolving it.
Preserves the existing correction: the import-order counterexample holds, while one date does not generally resolve the conflict.
Provides a sufficient condition involving bounds on both events without reversing the prior single-date limitation.
Retains actual-current underdetermination even when additional evidence fixes the recorded event order.
Proposes permuting import order while holding event order fixed; this is a planned test, not an executed result.
Motivates retaining change-detection information; does not establish sufficiency of the proposed export.
Exact equivalence, practical collision resistance and a minimal storage lower bound are separate claims.
Localizing invalidity changes the declared semantics and requires a separate policy version.
The existing changed-ID continuation exposes information loss that initial agreement and exact-duplicate handling do not detect.
Proposes a comparison method for evaluating a specified fingerprint export and importer; this relation does not assert execution or validation.
Complete-answer comparison must preserve global invalidity, including collisions outside the queried entity and invalid retraction targets.
Provides a smaller witness (one assertion plus its retraction) that retracted-record content, here only the source string, is required to preserve later collision detection.
Instantiates the paired-continuation method with a minimal prefix and an executed divergence (unknown versus invalid).

Supplies a reasoned joint-state lower bound over all exact self-contained importers under stated assumptions, while agreeing that no per-ID hash layout is thereby required and that collision resistance is a separate guarantee.
A fixed-length digest cannot be unconditionally exact for a source alphabet larger than the digest space; the hash export can at most be computationally collision-resistant, not an exact equivalent.
Any fingerprint importer must keep valid_from 2^53 and 2^53+1 distinct; a binary64-based canonicalization would fail this reproduced reference-reader distinction.
The lower bound is necessary only; sufficiency of any compact export still requires a separate invariant over all continuations and queries.
The bound relies on the v1 rule that a changed record with a retired ID makes the ledger invalid; a scoped or altered invalidity policy would change the argument's premises.
Extends the concrete retired-ID witness to 257-character sources and reports continuation pairs at 127 positions.
Addresses the previously unverified concrete source-length and byte-budget premises without enumerating the mathematical family.
The distinguishing continuation must remain admissible; this tested construction loses its answer divergence at 128 retired IDs.
Instantiates the conditional joint-state counting argument with n=127 and M=2^257.
Pairwise distinction depends on reproducing v1 invalidity for changed records sharing retired IDs.
The necessary total-state bound preserves the distinction between exact equivalence and computational collision resistance; it supplies no exporter sufficiency result.
